lines.en: Hannah, welcome to Toronto! English is spoken here, but French is used too.

lines.en: Yes, I read that both languages are used on signs.

lines.en: Right. This hotel is called the Maple Inn, and breakfast is served downstairs.

lines.en: Good. Is the room cleaned every day?
lines.pt: Bom. O quarto é limpo todos os dias?

lines.en: Yes, it is cleaned in the morning, and the towels are changed too.
lines.pt: Sim, é limpo de manhã, e as toalhas também são trocadas.

lines.en: And is the key card used for the lift?

lines.pt: Sim, é usado para a sua porta e o elevador. Chama-se “key card”.

lines.en: Perfect. Is the pool open at night?
lines.pt: Perfeito. A piscina fica aberta à noite?

lines.en: It is closed at ten, so let’s swim now.
lines.pt: Ela é fechada às dez, então vamos nadar agora.

facts.label: Passivo no presente (lugares)
facts.sub: Singular: is spoken. Plural: are used. Nome: is called. Serviços: is served / is cleaned. Pergunta: Is the room cleaned every day?

facts.label: É falado
facts.sub: Use is spoken para línguas. English is spoken here. Two languages are spoken at the front desk. O particípio de speak é spoken, não speaked.

facts.label: Se chama
facts.sub: Use is called para dar o nome de uma coisa ou lugar. The hotel is called the Maple Inn. It is called a “key card”. Em português, é “se chama”.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: “English is spoken here” is a present passive.
We use is called to give a name.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: “English is spoken here” is a present passive. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “Two languages is spoken”. → Falso (Plural: are spoken.)
We use is called to give a name. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A welcome at a Toronto hotel · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a sunny afternoon in downtown Toronto. Max arrives at a small hotel with two heavy bags. Gwen works at the front desk and speaks to him. Max visits Canada for the first time. He has many questions about the hotel. Gwen answers each one with a smile.

“Max, welcome to Toronto! English is spoken here, but French is used too.” says Gwen. “Yes, I read that both languages are used on signs.” says Max. “Right. This hotel is called the Maple Inn, and breakfast is served downstairs.” says Gwen.
